title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 93-95). Grothendieck is studying how Galois sections attached to rational points behave under specialization. The setting: a hyperbolic curve U_K over a field K of finite type, a model S of K, and a relative curve U ⊂ X over a dense open of S. The boundary S̄ \ S, or the locus where the point degenerates, has irreducible components D_α with generic points s_α.

A K-rational point of U_K gives a splitting of the extension π_1(U_K) → Gal_K, written E_{U_K} → E_K. The question is what happens at points s ∈ ∪D_α.

Previous page: over the generic point s_α of D_α one gets a relative curve U_{D_α} over (an open of) D_α. The geometric fibre U_{s_α} no longer has the specialized point as a rational point of U. The point has specialized to a point at infinity i_α ∈ X_{s_α} \ U_{s_α}, rational over k(s_α). One still has, essentially canonically, a 'relative inertia subgroup' L_i ⊂ π attached to i_α.

This page: what is relevant is the class of the splittings of E_{X_{s_α}} (or E_{U_{s_α}}) over E_{k(s_α)} that live in this relative inertia ('cuspidal' or 'sections at infinity'). In particular, those determined by a choice of uniformizer of O_{S̄,s_α}, i.e. a local equation of D_α near its generic point. Added note: the uniformizer matters only through its class in m_{s_α}/m_{s_α}^2. So the cuspidal section depends on a nonzero cotangent (equivalently normal) vector to D_α at s_α. In modern terms it is a tangential base point at the cusp i_α, with the tangent direction transported from the conormal of D_α in S̄ via the section.

Such sections specialize in an evident way to closed points of D_α at which:
- D_α is regular;
- the rational section of the normal (conormal) line bundle N_{D_α/S} defined by the uniformizer stays regular and invertible.
There the tangential datum extends.

He then proposes, but sets aside as 'less burning', the specialization at the remaining points: higher-codimension points such as intersections of D_α's, or points where the normal section has a zero or pole. That would need an analogous study of profinite group extensions. On p. 95 he explains why: it concerns only formal 'germs' of sections (completion along s_0) rather than global relative sections. He returns to sections coming from K-rational points, formula (29).
errors: No mathematical error visible. The claim that the cuspidal section depends on the uniformizer only via m/m^2 is correct at the level of tame Kummer classes. A uniformizer changed by a unit u congruent to 1 mod m changes the Kummer class by u^{1/n}, which is trivial over the residue field. Strictly, the residue class of u modulo m (an element of k(s_α)^*) does change the section, which is consistent with dependence on the line m/m^2.
Gap acknowledged by the author: behaviour at singular points of ∪D_α, and where the normal section degenerates, is not treated.

ideas.what: When a rational point of the generic curve specializes into the boundary of the fibre over a divisor D_α, the attached Galois section specializes to a cuspidal section at the point at infinity i_α, lying in the relative inertia L_i.
ideas.modern_name: Cuspidal sections / sections at infinity; specialization of sections to cusps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Longue Marche, 1981); later Nakamura, Stix ('Evidence for the section conjecture', cuspidal sections), Esnault–Wittenberg
ideas.where_published: Longue Marche (circulated 1981) discusses sections at infinity; this specific specialization discussion is in the unpublished notes

ideas.what: The cuspidal section depends on the choice of a local equation of D_α only through its class in m_{s_α}/m_{s_α}^2, i.e. a normal or tangent vector.
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points; tangential sections parametrized by the normal line
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'); Ihara–Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse explicitly in this form

ideas.what: Specialization of these tangential sections to closed points of D_α where D_α is regular and the induced rational section of N_{D_α/S} is regular and invertible.
ideas.modern_name: Specialization of tangential base points in families; log-geometric extension of the normal-vector datum
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in log-étale fundamental group theory (Kato, Illusie, Vidal) and in work on moduli tangential base points (Ihara–Nakamura, Nakamura)

ideas.what: Proposal to study specialization at higher-codimension points (crossings, degeneration of the normal section) via extensions of profinite groups; set aside.
ideas.modern_name: Specialization at normal-crossing strata / log points of rank ≥ 2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Log fundamental groups (Kato, Nakayama), Nakamura's work on degenerations

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly leaves open the specialization of (tangential) sections at points of D_α where D_α is singular or the normal section degenerates, i.e. higher-rank log strata. He judges it less urgent because it concerns only formal germs of sections.
missed.quote: On peut se proposer d'étudier ce qui se passe aux les autres points ... Mais cela me semble d'un intérêt moins brûlant
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A systematic treatment of how arithmetic-point sections degenerate to multi-tangential (rank ≥ 2 log) sections at crossings is relevant to the section conjecture over higher-dimensional bases. Log-geometric frameworks now exist, so this is partly but not fully covered.

deep.surprise_reason: The page anticipates the tangential-base-point picture: the cuspidal section depends on a vector in m/m^2, and the datum extends along D_α where the normal section of N_{D_α/S} is invertible. This predates Deligne's 1989 formalization in this arithmetic-specialization setting. Tangential base points and cuspidal sections are, however, well established, and Grothendieck's own Longue Marche discusses sections at infinity. So this is a notable but not startling unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'qui nous intéresse justement : regardons les classes de scindages, des E_{X_{s_α}} sur E_{k(s_α)}' rather than '...E_{X_B} sur E_{k(s)}'.
Line 3: 'relatif : c'est là — et notamment ceux relatifs aux choix d'une uniformisante de O_{S̄,s_α}'.

The inserted parenthesis reads approximately '(qui interviennent par le biais qu'elles définissent dans m_{s_α}/m_{s_α}^2)', attached to 'pt gén. s_α'; the struck-out word before it appears to be '(pt gén.)'.
'la section rationnelle associée du faisceau inversible N_{D_α/S} (si l'on suppose D_α régulier) reste régulière, et de N_{D_α/S} inversible' — '{+r+}' is a marginal insertion over N.
'pour les autres points — i.e. de dimension ≥ 2 [?] — la spécialisation des sections (d'extensions de groupes profinis), en faisant une étude analogue [?] à la précédente, pour cette question'.
'Mais cela me semble d'un intérêt moins brûlant — car cela n'est [plus une question ...]'.
